summary: Order quote timeouts originate in pricing-engine, not order-service or market-data-service. At 12:04 the feature-flag change cfg-3120 ramped flags.pricing.greeks_v2.rollout_pct from 5 to 100, routing all quotes through the GreeksV2 Monte-Carlo calculator (20000 paths, 3-9s per computation). pricing-engine CPU pinned at ~99%, quote p99 rose from ~60ms to ~2.6s, exceeding the 2000ms compute budget (94 'deadline exceeded' errors), which surfaced as 2500ms quote-call timeouts and ~8% errors in order-service from 12:06. The market-data-service protobuf deploy (dep-6111, 11:56) is exonerated: its latency and error rate never moved, and pricing-engine had no deployment. Root cause category: config_change. Recommend reverting cfg-3120 (roll greeks_v2 back to 5%) immediately.

ranked_hypotheses.title: greeks_v2 flag ramp made quote computation CPU-bound, saturating pricing-engine
ranked_hypotheses.statement: Config change cfg-3120 ramped pricing-engine's flags.pricing.greeks_v2.rollout_pct from 5 to 100 at 12:04, routing all quotes through the expensive GreeksV2 Monte-Carlo calculator (20000 paths, 3-9s each). This drove pricing-engine CPU to ~99%, pushing quote latency p99 to ~2.6s and exceeding the 2000ms compute budget, which propagated as 2500ms quote timeouts and ~8% errors in order-service. Fault originates in pricing-engine (triggered by a config/feature-flag change, not a release).

causal_chain.claim: All quotes now use GreeksV2 Monte-Carlo (20000 paths, 3-9s)
Quote p99 jumps to ~2.6s, exceeding 2000ms budget
order-service 2500ms quote calls time out, ~8% errors

assumptions: The 2000ms compute budget is a fixed config unrelated to the flag; the calculator choice (GreeksV2) is what changed

ranked_hypotheses.title: market-data-service protobuf deploy corrupted quote payloads
ranked_hypotheses.statement: dep-6111 (market-data-service v5.2.0 protobuf serialization, 11:56) caused quote failures by changing payload format for internal callers.
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: market-data-service latency (~40ms) and error rate (~0.2%) never moved (F9, F10); pricing-engine had no deployment (F13); the failures are compute-bound GreeksV2 Monte-Carlo runs (F4, F5) starting after the 12:04 config change, not payload/deserialization errors.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Load outgrew pricing-engine capacity
ranked_hypotheses.statement: A market-open traffic surge exceeded provisioned pricing-engine capacity, causing CPU saturation and timeouts (as in HIST-113).
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: pricing-engine request_rate stayed flat (~631->644 req/s, F8); demand never rose. What changed was per-request compute cost, driven by the greeks_v2 flag (F1), not load.

facts.statement: cfg-3120 ramped flags.pricing.greeks_v2.rollout_pct from 5 to 100 at 12:04:00Z.
pricing-engine p99 latency jumped from ~60ms to ~2600ms at the 12:00 bucket.
pricing-engine CPU jumped from ~40% to ~99% at the 12:00 bucket.
pricing-engine logs show GreeksV2Calculator Monte-Carlo runs of 20000 paths taking up to 8942ms.
pricing-engine logged 94 'request deadline exceeded computing quote (2000ms budget) calculator=GreeksV2' errors.
order-service logged 76 'pricing-engine quote call timed out after 2500ms' errors starting 12:06:10Z.
order-service error rate jumped from ~0.2% to ~8% at the 12:00 bucket.
pricing-engine request_rate remained flat (~631-644 req/s); no traffic surge.
market-data-service latency (~40ms) and error rate (~0.2%) never changed across the window.
The only deployment in the window is market-data-service dep-6111 (protobuf) at 11:56; pricing-engine had zero deployments.
pricing-engine memory stayed flat ~49%, so no memory leak/GC cause.
pricing-engine error rate rose to ~12.5% starting the 12:00 bucket.

assumptions: The 2000ms compute budget is fixed service config independent of the flag, so the calculator (GreeksV2) choice is the changed variable.
Order-service/quote traffic and exchange-gateway/external providers were healthy; no evidence of exchange-api degradation was found (its telemetry is unavailable).

timeline.event: pricing-engine CPU jumps to ~99% and p99 latency to ~2.6s (bucket).
Config change cfg-3120 ramps greeks_v2 rollout from 5% to 100%.
First order-service 'quote call timed out after 2500ms' error.
First 'request deadline exceeded computing quote (2000ms budget) calculator=GreeksV2'.

recommended_actions.action: Revert config cfg-3120: roll flags.pricing.greeks_v2.rollout_pct back to 5 (or 0) to restore fast quote computation.
recommended_actions.rationale: The flag ramp at 12:04 is the trigger; reverting removes the expensive Monte-Carlo path and should restore pricing-engine CPU/latency.

recommended_actions.action: Verify no other service deploys/config changes are pending; treat dep-6111 (market-data-service) as a red herring.
recommended_actions.rationale: MDS telemetry was flat, so rollback of dep-6111 is unnecessary and would be a distraction.

recommended_actions.action: Before re-enabling greeks_v2, add a cost/latency guard: cap Monte-Carlo paths or add a fast-fail + load test so a 5->100 ramp cannot pin CPU.
recommended_actions.rationale: The v2 calculator at 20000 paths exceeds the 2000ms budget even at normal request rates, so any full ramp will recur.

recommended_actions.action: Add gating/auto-rollback on feature-flag ramps tied to pricing-engine CPU and quote p99 SLOs.
recommended_actions.rationale: A gradual canary on the compute-heavy flag would have caught this before full rollout.

data_gaps: One config-audit shard (2/3) did not respond on the first call (tc-003, partial); a pricing-engine-scoped retry (tc-004) succeeded, but other services' config changes cannot be fully ruled out.
exchange-api (external vendor) has has_telemetry=false, so external-provider health could not be checked directly and remains an unverified alternative.
